$comment: The registry of scripts (CLAUDE.md 'Scripts are the hands'). Every file in scripts/ is listed here; `node scripts/scripts.mjs lint` enforces it. `node scripts/scripts.mjs search <words>` finds one by what it does. `external` lists scripts in the other repos that flix sessions use read-only.

scripts.name: scripts
scripts.does: Lists, searches and lints this manifest: the way to find out whether a script already exists before doing a thing by hand.

scripts.name: wiki
scripts.does: Searches, indexes and lints the wiki/ knowledge base; run `search` before reading pages by hand, `index` then `lint` after any wiki edit.

scripts.name: check
scripts.does: Runs the pre-commit checks in order (typecheck, the web's tsc, lint with the known-warning baseline, tests, optionally the image build) and stops at the first failure.
usage: node scripts/check.mjs            # typecheck, web tsc, lint, test
node scripts/check.mjs --docker   # plus docker build -t flix .
scripts.writes: nothing (docker build writes the local image flix)

scripts.name: deploy-check
scripts.does: After a push: waits for /healthz on the cluster to report the pushed sha, then GETs the smoke routes and prints each status, and with anything Unlisted fails if an Unlisted video is on Home, Featured or a normal video's related list, or noUnlisted does not shrink the library, and reports the Cast sync (fails if it errored); shows the deployment's image when kubectl is present. Read-only.
usage: node scripts/deploy-check.mjs             # waits for HEAD, up to 10 min
node scripts/deploy-check.mjs --no-wait   # report what runs now, no waiting

scripts.name: mobile-check
scripts.does: Headless Chrome at iPhone size: per page, reports horizontal overflow and saves a screenshot; blocks every write that would record viewing.

env.H: viewport height (956); W=932 H=430 is landscape

scripts.name: touch-check
scripts.does: Drives the player with real touch events in headless Chrome (tap, seek drag, bar tap, double tap, sideways swipe, centre play/pause) and prints the player state after each step; writes are blocked.

env.H: viewport height (956); W=932 H=430 is landscape

scripts.name: mini-check
scripts.does: Checks the mini-player round trip with real touch events in headless Chrome: play a scene, tap Home (docks), tap the docked picture, the title and Expand (each restores the full player), then tap a related card, go Back and tap it again (each opens on its own page, never docked); writes are blocked. Run it against a production build (vite preview): dev's StrictMode remount hides the scene-to-scene slot bug.
usage: node scripts/mini-check.mjs <outdir> http://localhost:5175 /scene/<id>   # after: pnpm --filter @flix/web exec vite build && FLIX_SERVER=http://flix.lan pnpm --filter @flix/web exec vite preview --port 5175 --strictPort
node scripts/mini-check.mjs <outdir> http://localhost:5174 /scene/<id>   # against Vite dev: the Home round trips only are meaningful

env.STEP: ms to wait after a tap (1500)

scripts.name: card-check
scripts.does: Checks drag-to-preview on scene cards in headless Chrome (a 25 px drag starts the preview without opening the video, a tap still opens it); writes are blocked.

scripts.name: stash-schema
scripts.does: Refreshes apps/server/stash.schema.graphql from a running Stash (or a saved introspection JSON) so codegen can regenerate stash.schema.ts after a Stash upgrade.

env.STASH_API_KEY: never printed; the user sets it

scripts.name: webkit-mini-check
scripts.does: The mini-player round trip in real WebKit (Playwright's build, iPhone emulation with touch): play, tap Home (docks), tap Expand, the title and the picture (each restores); prints console, page errors and failed requests; writes are blocked.

env.PLAYWRIGHT: path of the global playwright package (/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/playwright)

scripts.name: perf-check
scripts.does: Client performance per route in headless Chrome (phone or desktop): cold-load timing, requests and bytes by type, API call sequence, largest responses, first-screen image variant fit, CLS/LCP/long tasks, optional page-by-page scroll cost, then a second load for HTTP-cache hits; writes result.json; writes are blocked.
usage: DESKTOP=1 W=1440 H=900 node scripts/perf-check.mjs <outdir> http://localhost:5174 /browse

scripts.name: phone-flow
scripts.does: Step-driven headless Chrome at iPhone size: goto, tap, tapText, longpress, type, key, scroll, scrollTo, back, eval, shot, full-page shot, and `targets` (every visible control under 44 px with its size); writes are blocked; STUB answers chosen GET API paths with given JSON, to show a state production lacks.

env.STUB: JSON map of GET API pathname → JSON answer, stubbed in the browser (reads only)

scripts.name: desktop-check
scripts.does: Scenario-driven headless Chrome at desktop size: real mouse moves, clicks, right-clicks, key presses, Tab, typing, scroll, eval and screenshots per scenario; writes are blocked. Example scenario: scripts/examples/desktop-scenario.json.
usage: LATENCY=1500 node scripts/desktop-check.mjs <outdir> http://localhost:5174 <scenario.json>   # catch loading states

env.LATENCY: ms added to every /api and /media answer (0; Vite's modules are not delayed); with a scenario `wait` under it, the first shot catches skeletons and placeholders

scripts.name: api-latency
scripts.does: Times GET API routes (read-only) N times with the browser's Accept-Encoding: ms, gzip and raw bytes, Content-Encoding, Cache-Control, ETag, status and the Stash queries / asset fetches each sample caused (from GET /api/admin/cache); TSV on stdout. Built-in route list, or pass a file.

scripts.name: media-probe
scripts.does: Probes media proxy URLs twice each (read-only): status, ms, bytes, type, Cache-Control, ETag, Content-Length and whether the BFF went to Stash (asset counter delta); TSV on stdout.

scripts.name: whisparr
scripts.does: Whisparr v3 API client (moved from the nas repo's arr.py): ping, status, queue, history, wanted, logs, config, snapshot to private/ops/inventory/whisparr3/, raw get, and dry-run-by-default writes (set, put, post, delete, cmd).
usage: scripts/whisparr.py set performer/<id> whisparrMonitorNewItems=false   # dry run; add --apply
scripts.writes: Whisparr, only with --apply (Backup first unless --no-backup); snapshot writes private/ops/inventory/whisparr3/

scripts.name: stash
scripts.does: Stash GraphQL client (moved from the nas repo): ping, status, redacted config, job queue, and any query; a mutation is a dry run unless --apply.
scripts.writes: Stash, only for a mutation with --apply

scripts.name: privacy-check
scripts.does: Fails when a tracked or new file names a performer, studio or indexer from the library (the repo is mirrored publicly); history scans every line the commits in a range add (default github/main..HEAD, what the next mirror push publishes); refresh rebuilds the generated denylist from flix's API.
scripts.writes: refresh writes private/denylist.auto.txt; the check writes nothing

scripts.name: whisparr-sync
scripts.does: Runs the Whisparr guard on the flix server: every performer and studio in Whisparr is unmonitored, and a monitored scene stays monitored only if flix fetched it or it is downloading; prints the plan or the result. Dry run unless --apply.
scripts.writes: Whisparr monitoring flags, and flix's whisparr_watch and whisparr_gets rows, only with --apply

scripts.name: whisparr-cleanup
scripts.does: Deletes Whisparr scene records without a file unless downloading or grabbed, a waiting Get from flix or queued, then every studio and performer left with no scene record; never files, no import exclusion, never a record with a file; starts with a Whisparr Backup; runs on the flix server. Dry run unless --apply.
scripts.writes: Whisparr: a Backup, then deletes scene, studio and performer records (not files), only with --apply

scripts.name: library-reconcile
scripts.does: Reconciles the video files on disk with Stash and Whisparr: files Stash never scanned, files Whisparr does not track, records whose file is gone, Stash scenes without a StashDB id that Whisparr's folder name supplies, linked scenes Identify left bare, and ids that differ between the two. Runs inside the flix pod (keys and NFS mount there, no .env needed). Report only unless --scan (Stash scan of the unscanned folders), --link (set the ids, one Identify) or --fill (scrape bare linked scenes by id and write title, studio, performers, tags, cover).
usage: kubectl -n flix exec -i deploy/flix -- node - < scripts/library-reconcile.mjs
kubectl -n flix exec -i deploy/flix -- node - --scan < scripts/library-reconcile.mjs
kubectl -n flix exec -i deploy/flix -- node - --link < scripts/library-reconcile.mjs
kubectl -n flix exec -i deploy/flix -- node - --fill < scripts/library-reconcile.mjs

env.DISK_ROOT: the library mount to walk (default: the local side of MEDIA_PATH_MAP)

scripts.writes: Stash only, and only with a flag: --scan queues metadataScan for the unscanned folders; --link runs sceneUpdate(stash_ids) on the linkable scenes and queues metadataIdentify; --fill scrapes each bare linked scene from StashDB and runs sceneUpdate, creating missing studios, performers and tags. Whisparr is never written.
